## Summary

- Use the job-scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN` for progress comment creation, updates, cancellation, and final replacement.
- Keep resolved App/PAT credentials limited to deterministic lifecycle and fallback operations.
- Preserve created and edited human-comment triggers for the #455/#456 policy.
- Document why job-level bot filtering cannot prevent workflow-run creation.
- Add focused token-wiring, finalization, and trigger regression coverage.

## Tests

- `npm --prefix .agent run test:ci`

Closes #499

## Notes

- The core design is sound: progress creation, updates, cancellation, and final replacement use the non-recursive job token, while human `created` and `edited` triggers remain intact.
- An independent `npm --prefix .agent run test:ci` against head `006934548618c8bce845283e6fa40725ff783d93` passed all build, runtime, workflow, docs, and shell lanes.
- The smallest follow-up is to align fix-status cleanup with the job-token author and add coverage for both repeated-run cleanup and failed finalization fallback.

## Findings

- **WARNING:** The fix-PR finalizer supplies the resolved App/PAT as ambient `GH_TOKEN` but uses `github.token` to patch the current progress comment ([workflow](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/006934548618c8bce845283e6fa40725ff783d93/.github/workflows/agent-fix-pr.yml#L278-L298)). Cleanup filters old statuses to comments authored by its authenticated viewer ([filter](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/006934548618c8bce845283e6fa40725ff783d93/.agent/src/review-summary-minimize.ts#L201-L208)). Consequently, when App/PAT auth is configured, the next run will not collapse the prior `github-actions[bot]` status. The new finalization test disables cleanup, so it misses this interaction ([test](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/006934548618c8bce845283e6fa40725ff783d93/.agent/src/__tests__/post-comment-cli.test.ts#L311-L379)).
- **INFO:** Add a failure-path test showing that a workflow-token fetch or PATCH failure is logged and produces the normal App/PAT-authenticated fallback comment.

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: 006934548618c8bce845283e6fa40725ff783d93 -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #500 addresses #499 by moving progress-comment creation, updates, cancellation, and final replacement to the job-scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN`, preventing recursive Agent Entrypoint runs. App/PAT credentials remain limited to deterministic lifecycle and fallback operations and are no longer exposed to implement, fix-PR, or answer agents. The PR preserves human `created` and `edited` triggers required by #455/#456 and adds focused documentation and tests. The current head, `0069345`, has passing checks.

## Review

The core design is sound and no blocking defect was found. One reviewer considered the PR borderline `SHIP`, while two independent reviews identified the same repeated fix-run cleanup regression.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Repeated fix-PR statuses evade cleanup | WARNING | Finalized progress comments are now authored by `github-actions[bot]`, but cleanup still authenticates as the resolved App/PAT and only minimizes comments authored by that viewer. Repeated App-backed fix runs will therefore accumulate prior workflow-authored statuses. |
| Primary merged responses change author identity | INFO | Merged responses will display `github-actions[bot]` rather than the Sepo App identity. Reviewers considered this an inherent, acceptable tradeoff of the non-recursive design; fallback comments remain App-authored. |

## Progress

- The live PR head matches the head reviewed by all reviewers, and the current check passes.
- Reviewers verified the full `.agent` CI suite and confirmed that human edited-comment routing remains preserved.
- The existing top-level rubrics review already describes the cleanup regression, so no duplicate inline comment was posted; there are no inline comments or review threads.
- A workflow-token failure-path test was suggested as optional additional coverage; the existing implementation already logs merge failures and falls back to normal posting.
- Release notes remain untouched, consistent with the repository’s release-preparation policy.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Repeated fix-PR statuses evade cleanup</summary>

**Cause:** [`collapsePreviousFixPrComments`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/006934548618c8bce845283e6fa40725ff783d93/.agent/src/review-summary-minimize.ts#L201-L208) filters comments to the authenticated viewer. The [fix-PR finalizer](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/006934548618c8bce845283e6fa40725ff783d93/.github/workflows/agent-fix-pr.yml#L278-L298) runs cleanup with App/PAT authentication, then patches the current status with the workflow token.

**Candidate solutions:**

- Preserve the existing App/PAT cleanup for legacy statuses and add a workflow-token cleanup pass for `github-actions[bot]` statuses.
- Alternatively, add a narrowly scoped trusted-author mode limited to recognized fix-PR status markers, without permitting human or unrelated bot comments to be minimized.
- Add a repeated-run cross-identity regression test.

**Comments:** This does not undermine the recursion fix, but it regresses the configured old-status cleanup behavior.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step

`FIX_PR`: The cleanup regression has a focused branch-level fix and regression test that are safe for an automated fix pass.

## Final Verdict

MINOR_ISSUES

## Action Items

- [ ] Preserve cleanup for both legacy App/PAT-authored and new workflow-authored fix-PR statuses, while retaining protections for human and unrelated-bot comments, and add cross-identity regression coverage.

The original bug is that App-authored progress-comment edits spawned recursive Agent Entrypoint runs—48 extra runs were observed from two `/answer` jobs ([#499](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/499)). PR #500 fixes that with the non-recursive job `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

The remaining review issue is an identity mismatch:

- New `/fix-pr` statuses are authored by `github-actions[bot]`.
- Old-status cleanup authenticates as the Sepo App/PAT and only collapses comments authored by that identity.
- Repeated `/fix-pr` runs can therefore leave stale status comments accumulating.

The core recursion fix works and CI passes; this is a minor cleanup/idempotency regression.

To fix it, send:

`@sepo-agent /fix-pr preserve cleanup of both App/PAT-authored and github-actions[bot] fix-pr statuses, with cross-identity regression coverage`
